reviewer: Pickle: official-source winter car battery jump starter comparison
method: Reviewed the full draft against official sources. Korea Transportation Safety Authority official blog (2020-02-04): Insurance Development Institute figures of about 15 million emergency dispatch calls a year, about 1.7 million in December, roughly 50 percent from battery discharge; 2017 winter experiment with a 4-year-old battery at -18 C, 12-hour parking: 12.53 V at room temperature, 12.04 V at -18 C without accessories, 1.8 V with a dashcam on constant power and no start; best battery temperature 25-30 C, 14 V or more with engine running considered healthy, 12 V or below declining, 2.13 V x 6 cells, indicator green/black/white. National Tax Service regional notice (2022-01-05) citing KOTSA: battery performance drops up to 40 percent below zero, dashcam and navigation on long-term parking cause discharge. Korea Road Traffic Authority official blog (2024-12-03): winter breakdowns number one battery discharge, electrolyte optimum at 25 C, symptoms (slow cranking, warning lamp, dim headlights), replacement cycle 3-4 years, prevention (indoor parking, weekly 10-minute drive, lights check, electronics off 5 minutes before arrival), jump order with red to plus terminals and black to the dead car's engine block as ground. Kia 2026 owner manual (SP3) and Hyundai 2026 owner manual (DN8): 12 V only, never jump a frozen or low-electrolyte battery, plus clamps must not touch each other, negative clamp grounded to solid metal away from the battery because direct connection risks explosion, battery acid contact washed with clean water for about 15 minutes, disconnection in reverse order (negative first), keep the engine running for a while after a jump. ATLASBX (Hankook and Company, 2021-07-27): replacement recommended within 3 years or about 50,000 km, charging voltage 13.6-14.2 V with engine on, about 9.5 V during cranking means end of life, CCA defined at -18 C with 600 A or more recommended for winter, manufacturer insulation pad helpful. Financial News consumer campaign (2022-12-23): below -10 C discharges become frequent, dim dashboard lighting signals discharge, start the engine 1-2 times a week during long parking, switch dashcam to parking mode. Korea Consumer Agency press release (2025-12-02, no=1003970724): of 12 lithium-ion power banks tested, 4 (33.3 percent) suffered protection-circuit damage in overcharge testing, 4 of 12 lacked charger-related warnings, of 462 surveyed users 57.6 percent (266) did not know a matching rated charger matters; consumers told to use the rated charger, unplug promptly after full charge, and keep combustibles away while charging. Yonhap (2025-12-02) adds product detail of the same survey. National Fire Agency policy briefing (korea.kr, 2025-07-15): 678 lithium-ion battery fires in 2020-2024, rising from 98 to 117 a year, main causes overcharge, impact damage, and high-temperature storage; use KC-certified genuine batteries and chargers, unplug promptly when full, avoid charging while out or asleep, store away from direct sunlight and moisture. Korea Fire Insurance Association webzine no. 101: a parked car under direct sun can exceed 90 C inside, so storing or charging batteries there or in any space at 60 C or above is dangerous; over-discharge left unattended can disable protection circuits. Consumer Reports Jump-Starter Buying Guide (updated 2026-10): peak-amp selection by engine size (800-1,200 A under 2.0 L, 1,200-2,000 A for 2.0-3.0 L, 2,000-3,000 A over 3.0 L, at least 3,000 A for diesels), reverse-polarity/short-circuit/overcurrent protection wanted, storage temperature limits and glovebox/trunk storage away from sun. Korea Road Corporation official blog (2022-02-22): winter emergency calls over 60 percent battery charging for one insurer across 3 years, 562 highway discharge dispatches in 2021, wait about 5 minutes connected before starting, 10-20 minutes of charging for long-parked batteries, same-voltage pairs only, reverse-order removal. Product figures from three Coupang product pages verified in-browser on 2026-11-01: Pullaros emergency-start power bank jump starter with smart jumper cable and pouch, 14800 mAh, 1 set at 59,000 KRW (53 percent off 128,000, product 7346410603, about 2,681 reviews on the Coupang search list); 12 V 6A pulse-repair LCD smart car/motorcycle battery charger at 17,890 KRW (28 percent off 25,000, 187 reviews, product 7778381144, seller Green, 12 V 4Ah-100Ah); Coms cigarette-socket voltage tester BD917, 1 pc at 6,100 KRW (12 percent off 7,000, product 237647073). Derived calculations recorded in research: charger plus voltmeter costs 23,990 KRW, 35,010 KRW less than the jump starter; the 2017 experiment shows a 0.49 V drop from cold alone versus a 10.73 V drop with a constant-power dashcam, a 10.24 V difference over the same 12 hours. Plan deviations: the plan's KOTSA figures of a 12.4-12.8 V resting norm, 9.6-10 V cranking discharge threshold, 30-50 percent cold capacity loss, and 3-4 year or 50,000-60,000 km replacement were only partially confirmed; sources actually state a 40 percent performance drop below zero, 12.53 V resting reference, 13.6-14.2 V charging range, 9.5 V cranking replacement signal, and 3 years/50,000 km replacement, so the guide uses the verified figures and says so. The plan's ECU 3-million-won reverse-voltage claim could not be verified in a primary source, so the guide describes the reverse-voltage risk qualitatively from the owner-manual grounding and touch prohibitions without a specific repair cost. The plan's National Fire Research Institute source was replaced with the NFA policy briefing and the Fire Insurance Association study, which carry the same storage-safety points.
